topics.topic: Define how CLK-002 tests prove clock readings and rate-limit window state remain process-local
questions: What must the CLK-002 Required test show to establish that monotonic readings and viewer-entry window state never cross a process boundary?

quotes:
- CLK-002: elapsed durations are measured only through the clock source's
  monotonic reading, one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request; they
  are used within one process, never persisted,
  and never compared with or mixed into wall-clock values.

- CLK-002: a test showing that the elapsed durations the portal measures
  (the A25 viewer-entry window) come from the clock source's monotonic
  reading, one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request, are not persisted, and are not compared with or mixed into
  wall-clock values.
judgement.why: The process-local invariant and its Required tests item are unchanged in the closed and current texts, and the change to A28 did not make this omission newly matter.

topics.topic: Define how CLK-002 tests prove the rate limiter is the sole caller of the monotonic clock
questions: What must the CLK-002 Required test do to demonstrate that the viewer-entry rate limit is the only caller of the clock source’s monotonic reading?

quotes:
- the elapsed clock gives a duration scale: one reading per call of a
  clock that cannot move backwards, in seconds as a float, the same value
  `time.monotonic()` gives. Its one user is the viewer-entry rate limit of
  A25, which takes one reading per viewer-entry request and measures its
  window with it; a reading is never stored, never turned into an instant
  and never ordered against a persisted record.

- CLK-002: elapsed durations are measured only through the clock source's
  monotonic reading, one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request; they
  are used within one process, never persisted,
  and never compared with or mixed into wall-clock values. Owners: the
  clock source, as the only reader of the monotonic clock; the viewer-entry
  rate limit of A25, for its one reading per request and its window.

- CLK-001: a test per operation that reads the current time — writing a
  timestamp or comparing it with a stored one, expiry checks included —
  with the clock source fixed at a known instant, showing that the
  operation reads it once and uses that instant for every comparison, that
  its portal-owned event timestamps equal that instant, that a derived
  expiry equals that instant plus the TTL, and that supplied times and
  dates are stored as supplied; and that no module other than the clock
  source reads the host wall or monotonic clock directly.

- CLK-002: a test showing that the elapsed durations the portal measures
  (the A25 viewer-entry window) come from the clock source's monotonic
  reading, one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request, are not persisted, and are not compared with or mixed into
  wall-clock values.
judgement.divergence: One verification implementation inspects every caller of the clock source and rejects any monotonic consumer other than the A25 viewer-entry limiter; another exercises only the viewer-entry window and accepts an additional transient consumer, which the architecture verifier or a maintainer notices.
judgement.why: The new sole-user rule is not matched by a Required tests obligation to demonstrate that no other module calls the clock source's monotonic reading.

witness.initial: The viewer-entry limiter takes one clock-source monotonic reading per entry request, and the CLK-002 test verifies its window, persistence, and wall-clock separation requirements.
events: An implementer adds another module that calls the clock source's monotonic reading for transient performance measurement without persisting or mixing the value with wall-clock time.
The CLK-002 verification is run against the implementation.
outcomes: A verification that treats the sole-user rule as an exhaustive caller constraint rejects the implementation.
A verification limited to the properties expressly listed in the CLK-002 Required tests item exercises the viewer-entry window and accepts the implementation.
witness.observer: The architecture verifier and a maintainer adding the second consumer.

topics.topic: Define which requests count as viewer-entry attempts for the one-reading rule
questions: What exactly counts as a viewer-entry request for the one-reading rule: every HTTP attempt at the entry endpoint, only requests that reach the viewer-entry use case, or only attempts that pass parsing and preliminary validation?

quotes: install_transport_guards: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST register exactly one FastAPI http middleware on the supplied application. For every request the middleware MUST evaluate the checks below in the order they are written, and the order is a pipeline rather than a choice between alternatives: each check either produces the response named for it and ends the request there, or leaves the request untouched for the next check to evaluate. A check that does not produce a response MUST NOT call the next handler, MUST NOT return, and MUST NOT cause any later check to be skipped; the next handler is called exactly once, after every check in the list has left the request unrefused. The checks are: derive a request id carrying no identity or credential material; reject the request with 400 when _host_allowed refuses the request host against settings.trusted_hosts; answer an OPTIONS request carrying an Origin listed in settings.allowed_origins with a 204 preflight echoing the requested method and headers plus Vary Origin, together with the allow-origin and allow-credentials headers every allowed-origin response carries, and reject an unlisted origin with 403; reject POST on the canonical viewer logout path /auth/viewer/logout with 403 unless _normalized_origin of the request Origin equals _normalized_origin of settings.public_origin; reject with 413 when _body_within_limit refuses the declared Content-Length against settings.max_request_body_bytes; reject with 429 when _record_viewer_entry_attempt refuses a POST on the canonical viewer entry path /auth/viewer/enter, keyed by _client_bucket_key, before any credential parsing or verification. A POST to /auth/viewer/logout whose Origin is accepted therefore still passes through the body-size check, and so does every other request that is not refused before it. It MUST supply _record_viewer_entry_attempt with one reading of monotonic_seconds per entry attempt, a clock that cannot move backwards, never with wall-clock time and never with a host clock read directly, so that adjusting the system clock cannot widen the window or discard recorded attempts. Every response it produces or forwards, including each rejection above, MUST pass through _apply_security_headers with the request id and the _requires_no_store decision for the canonical path, and MUST carry the CORS allow-origin, allow-credentials and Vary headers only when the request Origin is listed in settings.allowed_origins. When settings.production_logging is true it MUST emit exactly one INFO record per completed request, built only by _transport_log_record. It MUST classify every path through _canonical_path so a deployment-prefixed path is treated exactly like its stripped inner path, keep its rate-limit state bounded inside the installed guard, and MUST NOT authenticate a principal, read persistence, import a domain or application module, or import starlette directly.
judgement.why: The later contract makes an entry attempt a POST on the canonical viewer-entry path that reaches the rate-limit check after the preceding transport checks and requires its monotonic reading before credential parsing or verification.
